tools.name: request_access
tools.description: Ask a human for access to this server. Returns an approveUrl and a userCode: show BOTH to the person you are working with, ask them to open the link and check that the code on the page matches, then call poll_access. When the client supports URL elicitation, call poll_access with urlMode=true instead of pasting the link into chat; clients without it keep this complete text fallback. The link grants nothing by itself — keep the deviceSecret this returns, it is what collects the token. Use this when a call answered 'authorization_required', or when your token stopped working (a server restart drops every grant).

tools.name: poll_access
tools.description: Collect the outcome of a request_access, proving possession of its deviceSecret. It HOLDS THE CALL OPEN and answers the moment the human decides — one call instead of a dozen, since each poll here costs a whole round trip through you. It waits 8 seconds by default; pass waitSeconds (up to 30) if your client tolerates a longer call. Pass urlMode=true when the client supports URL elicitation: while the request is pending this returns the standard -32042 URL-elicitation-required error, and retrying the same call after the browser decision returns the outcome. A wait that times out answers status=pending, and you simply call again. Then approved (with the token) or denied/expired. Use the token on every later call: as the X-Compose-Preview-Token header where you control headers, and otherwise as each gated tool's 'token' argument — which is what an MCP client reaching this flow mid-session needs, since its headers were fixed when it connected.

tools.name: catalog_render_preview
tools.description: Render one preview. Like local compose-ai-tools, the default semantics observation is token-frugal; request observe=png for pixels, observe=svg for the compose/figma-svg vector export as SVG source, or observe=scroll-png / observe=scroll-svg for the full-page capture of a scrollable screen rather than the viewport crop. Watch face previews also accept structured 'complications', 'watchFace', 'ambient', 'previewTime' / 'clockEpochMillis', and 'wfRenderer' ('dwf-rc' or 'dwf-apk'). 'watchFace' is the state the preview's own face is drawn in, never a face of its own: 'ambient', 'previewTime' (HH:mm, HH:mm:ss or epoch millis), 'clockEpochMillis', 'is24Hour', sensor values ('batteryPercent', 'stepCount', 'heartRate', ...), 'configurations' (UserConfiguration id to option) and 'themeColors'. Any other key, such as 'xml' or 'designId', is refused; a UI Builder design is seen on the real runtime in its Native pane. 'dwf-apk' runs the Android watch-face runtime and is refused with catalog_native_render_disabled where this server has turned that off; the default is then 'dwf-rc'; see each preview's watchFaceRenderers. Overrides, other observations and fresh renders require live grant scope; without it, a call with no overrides returns the published snapshot (as resources/read does).

tools.name: ui_builder_validate_watch_face
tools.description: Check what a watch-face design (a `wff-watchface` catalog design) costs on a watch, with Google's own validators: the WFF schema, the memory footprint and the Watch Face Push checks a watch runs before it installs a face. Returns `passed` and one entry per check with its findings; each finding carries a `suggestion` saying what to change. The `memory-footprint` check's `memory` is the face's decoded size against `activeLimitBytes` and `ambientLimitBytes`, and its `contributors` list the resources that cost the most (pixel size, decoded bytes, the size each is drawn at). Keep both modes under their limits: downscale an image to the size it is drawn at, and give ambient a dim or reduced variant rather than the full-colour one. A bitmap the face names that the design does not pin fails `bundle-resources`; pin it with ui_builder_put_asset. Validation is explicit: nothing else runs it, not an edit, a read or a publish. It runs the full packager, so call ui_builder_validate_watch_face when an edit pass is done and before ui_builder_publish_watch_face, not after every edit; an unchanged face answers from cache. The server runs one validation at a time and limits each account, so a busy or rate-limited call answers `watch_face_validation_busy` or `watch_face_validation_rate_limited` with `retryAfterSeconds`; wait that long. The per-edit `watchFaceCost` is the cheap estimate: every ui_builder_apply, ui_builder_replace_design_document and ui_builder_put_asset on a watch face already replies with it, an estimate of the same budgets (`active` and `ambient` as `usedBytes`, `limitBytes`, `percentOfLimit`), the `topContributors` with what to do about each, and the estimate's `errors`; read it after each edit and fix what it flags before building further. A failing face is a report with `passed: false`, not an error. A host whose operator left Google's validators off answers `watch_face_validation_disabled`.

revision.description: The revision to validate. Defaults to the current one.

tools.name: ui_builder_preview_catalog_recovery
tools.description: Dry-run recovery of a design whose stored catalog pin no longer resolves (`catalogUnavailable` from ui_builder_get_design). The server selects the exact currently served pin for the same catalog system and returns a CatalogUpgradePreviewV1: `status` (`ready` or `blocked`), `changes`, `issues`, and the hashes the move is checked against. This call never writes. When `status` is `ready` the reply also carries `apply`: the complete arguments for ui_builder_apply — send that object as they are and the design moves onto the served pin, recorded as a new revision. Assembled by hand it is `operations: [{"type":"upgradeCatalog", sourceCatalogPin, targetCatalogPin, sourceDocumentHash, targetDocumentHash, previewDigest}]` with `baseRevision` set to the preview's `baseRevision`, where `targetDocumentHash` is the preview's `candidateDocumentHash` and the other four are copied by name. A `blocked` preview has no `apply`: its error-severity `issues` say what the served catalog no longer accepts. The candidate document itself is omitted, since it is the whole design again; `includeCandidate: true` returns it.

tools.name: ui_builder_apply
tools.description: Apply design mutations — insertNode, setProperty, deleteNode, moveNode and the rest of DesignMutationV1 — as one operation. `baseRevision` is the revision you read; the outcome reports conflicts or rejected edits. This is how an agent adds a scaffold, fills its slots and sets modifiers. Use `setStateVariable` with `name` and `declaration` to add or edit state, `removeStateVariable` with `name` to remove unused state, and `setEventBinding` with `nodeId`, `event` and an ordered `actions` array to edit behavior. An empty actions array removes the event handler. These are the same edits as Screen > State and Properties > Actions in the browser. `removeNodeProperty` (or a setProperty whose value is `{"type":"null"}`) unsets the property — the way back after trying one — and is refused, naming the node and the field, when the catalog requires it. When somebody has commented on the design and you have not acknowledged it, the outcome carries a `comments` block naming the threads waiting on you; read it, because it is somebody talking about what you are editing. To recover a design whose catalog pin stopped resolving, send the `apply` object ui_builder_preview_catalog_recovery returns: one `upgradeCatalog` mutation, alone in its batch, at the preview's `baseRevision`, with the preview's `candidateDocumentHash` as its `targetDocumentHash`.
